So
CEDAR is a combination of things.
cues.zh: CEDAR 是几样东西的组合。

cues.en: It's both a language,
also called CDER Mesa, a programming language.
cues.zh: 也叫 CDER Mesa，一种编程语言。

cues.en: When people asked about it back in the eighties, we used to tell them it's kind of industrial strength Pascal.
cues.zh: 八十年代有人问起它时，我们常说它像是工业级的 Pascal。

cues.en: That

cues.zh: 能让你大致感受它的语法是什么样。而且

cues.zh: 后面我们会多聊聊 CDER 语言。

a set of libraries that people could build on.
cues.zh: 一组人们可以基于其构建的库。

cues.en: CDER was a very successful experience in code reuse.
cues.zh: CDER 在代码复用方面是一次非常成功的实践。

cues.en: The way that the CDER programming language works,
cues.zh: CDER 编程语言的工作方式，

cues.zh: 几乎强制你把代码打包成别人能用的形式，而别人也确实用了。

cues.en: There were dozens of people in the CEDAR community, and we were constantly building software on top of each other's,
cues.zh: CEDAR 社区里有几十个人，我们一直在彼此的基础上构建软件，

So
it was a pioneer
for the modular programming kind of paradigm?
cues.zh: 是模块化编程范式的先驱？

cues.en: Yes. I think that's fair to say.
cues.zh: 是的，我觉得这么说很合理。

cues.en: Certainly
very modular.
People built a lot of different kinds of applications on it. We were just talking about some of them.
cues.zh: 人们基于它构建了很多不同种类的应用。我们刚才还聊到其中一些。

cues.en: So there were
document processing tools,
there were email readers,
there was all kinds of
debugging tools,
publication,
two dimensional graphics, three-dimensional graphics, VLSI design tools,
cues.zh: 二维图形、三维图形、VLSI 设计工具，

cues.en: databases,
the list went on and on, networking, software.
cues.zh: 名单还长着呢，网络、软件。

cues.en: It was all done in CEDAR.
cues.zh: 全都是用 CEDAR 做的。

cues.en: And because,
because it was a fairly close knit community
cues.zh: 因为这是一个相当紧密的社区

cues.en: and because of the way the programming environment itself worked,
cues.zh: 也因为编程环境本身的运作方式，

cues.en: you could constantly be building on other people's software and even sometimes you would discover a bug in someone else's software and rather than bother them with it you would just fix it.
cues.zh: 你可以不断在别人的软件上构建，甚至有时发现别人软件里的 bug，也不会去打扰他们，而是直接修掉。

cues.en: And it meant that if
you found something wrong and you couldn't fix it yourself,
cues.zh: 你发现问题但自己修不了，

cues.en: it was easy to find out who was responsible for that and get a problem fixed quickly. And
cues.zh: 也很容易找出谁负责，并快速修好问题。而且

cues.en: what was the goal for
the
group that developed CEDAR? What were they trying to do with the environment?
cues.zh: 开发 CEDAR 的团队？他们想用这个环境做什么？

Park put a large
investment of time and effort into CDER. And one of the reasons they did that was this feeling that
cues.zh: 的时间和精力到 CDER 上。他们这样做的一个原因是觉得

cues.en: whatever we were going to do research on
in the CEDAR community,
that
we wanted to be able to do it very productively.
cues.zh: 希望能非常高效地去做。

cues.en: We wanted to stay on the cutting edge of whatever research topics we were working on. And in order to do that, we needed to have a programming environment that was very productive to work in.
cues.zh: 我们希望始终处在所研究课题的前沿。为此，我们需要一个能高效工作的编程环境。

cues.en: CEDAR was very successful at that.
cues.zh: CEDAR 在这一点上非常成功。

cues.zh: 显然，这些语言大不相同，它们所能实现的功能也截然不同。所以

interactive
way of working.
InterLisp,
because
of the way the Lisp language is with
cues.zh: 关于 Lisp 语言对于……的处理方式

cues.zh: 语法非常简单，你可以先生成代码，然后立即运行生成的代码。

a strongly typed language
with
separation between interfaces and implementations,

cues.zh: 正如我所说，这意味着它极其……

the code that you produced was
fairly robust and likely to,
if it compiled, was probably going to run. And
cues.zh: 只要编译通过，基本就能跑。而且

it was a good environment for building things that
cues.zh: 那是一个很适合构建东西的环境，那些……

cues.en: were easy to productize
because you already had them implemented in a language
cues.zh: 因为你已经在某种语言里实现了它们

fairly robust hardened code.
